questions.q: Who does Yahweh tell to listen to his message?
questions.a: He tells the people of Israel, the house of Israel, to listen.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people of Israel should not do?
questions.a: He says they should not act like the people of other nations, and they should not be terrified by things they see in the sky.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the customs of the other nations?
questions.a: He says they are worthless; for example, a craftsman cuts down a tree from the forest and carves an idol from it.

questions.q: How do people decorate and secure the idols they make?
questions.a: They decorate them with silver and gold and fasten them with nails so they will not fall over.

questions.q: What does Yahweh compare the idols to, and what can they not do?
questions.a: He compares them to scarecrows in a field of cucumbers; they cannot speak, walk, harm anyone, or help anyone.

questions.q: What does the prophet say about Yahweh’s greatness?
questions.a: He says there is no one like Yahweh; Yahweh is great, and his name is great in power.

questions.q: What does the prophet call Yahweh, and how should everyone respond to him?
questions.a: He calls Yahweh the king of the nations, and says everyone should honor him because there is no one like him among all the wise people of the nations.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about people who seek instruction from a wooden idol?
questions.a: He says they are altogether foolish, because seeking instruction from a wooden idol is useless.

questions.q: Where do the silver and gold used to make idols come from?
questions.a: The silver comes from Tarshish, and the gold comes from Uphaz.

questions.q: What does the prophet say about Yahweh in contrast to the idols?
questions.a: He says Yahweh is the true and living God and the eternal king, and the earth shakes when he is angry.

questions.q: What message does Yahweh tell the people of Israel to give about the false gods?
questions.a: They should say that the gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will disappear from the earth.

questions.q: What does the prophet say Yahweh did by his power, wisdom, and understanding?
questions.a: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.

questions.q: What happens when Yahweh speaks, according to this verse?
questions.a: The sky makes a loud noise with rain, clouds rise over the earth, and Yahweh sends lightning and wind.

questions.q: What does this verse say about every metalworker and the idols they make?
questions.a: Every metalworker is ashamed of his idols because they are not real gods and have no life in them.

questions.q: What will happen to the idols, according to this verse?
questions.a: They are worthless and deserve to be mocked, and they will perish when Yahweh punishes them.

questions.q: How is Yahweh, the inheritance of Jacob, different from the idols?
questions.a: He is not like the idols because he formed all things, and the people of Israel belong to him as his inheritance.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people of Jerusalem to do because enemies surround their city?
questions.a: He tells them to gather their belongings into a bundle and prepare to leave.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the people who live in the land at this time?
questions.a: He says he will expel them from the land and cause them to experience great trouble and pain.

questions.q: How does the prophet describe his own suffering?
questions.a: He says it is as though he has been badly wounded, but he must endure this suffering.

questions.q: What does the prophet say will happen to the tents and children of his people?
questions.a: He says their tents will be destroyed and their ropes torn apart, and their children will go away and not return.

questions.q: What does this verse say about the leaders of the people?
questions.a: It says the leaders are foolish and do not seek Yahweh, so they have not prospered, and the people they lead have been scattered.

questions.q: What is coming from the land of the north, and what will it do to the cities of Judah?
questions.a: A great noise from an army is coming from the north, and it will make the cities of Judah a desolate place where jackals live.

questions.q: What does the prophet say he knows about a person’s life?
questions.a: He knows that no person controls what happens to him, and no one can direct his own steps.

questions.q: How does the prophet ask Yahweh to correct him?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to correct him with justice and not in anger, so that he will not die.

questions.q: What does the prophet ask Yahweh to do to the nations that do not know him?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to pour out his anger on them, because they have destroyed the people of Jacob and made their land a desolate, uninhabited place.

commentary.text: The absurdity of idolatry. (Jer. 10:1-16) Destruction denounced against Jerusalem. (Jer. 10:17-25)

Jer. 10:1-16 The prophet shows the glory of Israel's God, and exposes the folly of idolaters. Charms and other attempts to obtain supernatural help, or to pry into futurity, are copied from the wicked customs of the heathen. Let us stand in awe, and not dare provoke God, by giving that glory to another which is due to him alone. He is ready to forgive, and save all who repent and believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ. Faith learns these blessed truths from the word of God; but all knowledge not from that source, leads to doctrines of vanity.

Jer. 10:17-25 The Jews who continued in their own land, felt secure. But, sooner or later, sinners will find all things as the word of God has declared, and that its threatenings are not empty terrors. Submission will support the believer under every grief allotted to him; but what can render the load of Divine vengeance easy to be borne by those who fall under it in sullen despair? Those cannot expect to prosper, who do not, by faith and prayer, take God with them in all their ways. The report of the enemy's approach was very dreadful. Yet the designs which men lay deep, and think well formed, are dashed to pieces in a moment. Events are often overruled, so as to be quite contrary to what we intended and expected. If the Lord has directed our steps into the ways of peace and righteousness, let us entreat him to enable us to walk therein. Say not, Lord, do not correct me; but, Lord, do not correct me in anger. We may bear the smart of God's rod, but we cannot bear the weight of his wrath. Those who restrain prayer, prove that they know not God; for those who know him will seek him, and seek his favour. If even severe corrections lead sinners to be convinced of wholesome truths, they will have abundant cause for gratitude. And they will then humble themselves before the Lord.
